card.name: Right after a brand drug name
card.fires_on: The word or word piece right after a brand-name drug used as the subject or object, such as 'is', 'should', 'be', or the last piece of the name. Seen in prescribing-information sentences about use, reduction or interaction.

modes.label: Verb after brand name
modes.description: A helper verb like is or should directly follows an uppercase brand name as the subject.
modes.example: Intervention SYMBRAVO<< is>> contraindicated in patients taking MA

modes.label: End of drug name
modes.description: The last piece of a brand or generic drug name just before a noun like dose, infusion or diluted.
modes.example: consider increasing the meper<<idine>> dosage until stable drug effects are achieved.

card.plain: It fires on the spot just after a drug's name is written in a label sentence, where the next word is usually a verb or dose noun.
